The 2019 Tour de Wallonie was a professional road cycling stage race that took place in the Wallonia region of Belgium from July 27 to July 31, 2019. It was the 46th edition of the race and was part of the UCI Europe Tour.

The race consisted of five stages, with a total distance of approximately 858 kilometers. The stages varied in length and difficulty, with some stages favoring sprinters and others featuring challenging climbs.

The overall winner of the 2019 Tour de Wallonie was Loïc Vliegen from Belgium, who won the race by just one second ahead of the second-place finisher, Quinn Simmons from the United States. Vliegen also won the points classification, while the mountains classification was won by Peter Kennaugh from Great Britain.

The 2019 Tour de Wallonie featured a strong field of riders from around the world, including several WorldTour teams. The race is known for its challenging parcours and often serves as a preparation race for the upcoming UCI World Tour races.

Overall, the 2019 Tour de Wallonie was a competitive and exciting race that showcased the beauty and challenges of the Wallonia region of Belgium.
